items.title: ‘People scared of economics’: Sarthak Pradhan on your money, GST and Fiscal Fables
items.summary: Why does it cost the government Rs 3 to raise Rs 1 in tax? Why does India spend only about 3 percent of its money at the local level, when China spends around 50 percent? And should governments be in the business of making soap and selling alcohol? Abhinandan Sekhri talks to Sarthak Pradhan, co-author of Fiscal Fables: A Citizen’s Guide to Public Finance (with Pranay Kotasthane), about how the government earns and spends your money. The book explains public finance through stories, movies and pop culture, with no equations. They cover taxes, GST, freebies, the Planning Commission, trade, and the cost of Delhi’s traffic and pollution. Whether you’ve read an economics book or not, this conversation is about your money. If you liked this video, let our reporters tell you why you should subscribe to Newslaundry .

items.title: Chennai rains: T Nagar, Velachery and other areas face waterlogging
items.summary: Heavy intermittent rainfall since Tuesday night, October 20, has caused waterlogging in several Chennai neighbourhoods, including T Nagar, Velachery, Nungambakkam, Ashok Nagar, and West Mambalam. The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has deployed motor pumps, tractors, and other machinery to remove stagnant rainwater. Civic workers have also been working on clearing blockages in drains and directing the water into the stormwater drain network. In T Nagar, rainwater accumulated on several major roads, including Panagal Park Road and Habibullah Road, as well as streets adjoining Thirumalai Road. Panagal Park Road, an important stretch connecting Anna Salai to T Nagar, was severely waterlogged. Two-wheelers, buses, autorickshaws, and cars struggled to navigate the road, with water reaching halfway up some vehicles. Traffic along this stretch has also been affected by ongoing Metro Rail construction on one side and stormwater drain works on the other. Bazullah Road and streets adjoining Thirumalai Road were also affected. Waterlogging was reported on GN Chetty Road too, where infrastructure works had been undertaken under the Smart City project.
